### 1 of 1. 1 field name in src/api/profile.ts breaks the naming rule

### What was found
The service sends data back to outside apps. One field name in that data is written `displayName` instead of `display_name`. It is at line 18 of src/api/profile.ts: `return { displayName: profile.name };`. No other card touches this file.

### Why it matters
The project rule says field names in data sent back to outside apps use lowercase words joined by underscores. The rule is in AGENTS.md, API naming.

### What happens if you accept
The fix would rename `displayName` to `display_name`. Apps that read `displayName` today would stop finding it. That breaks what the service promises to those apps, so this run cannot make the fix. Picking Ticket changes nothing now. You approve the ticket's exact wording before it is filed, and it records the rename as a planned change.

Pick one:
1. [ ] Fix - unavailable: the rename would break apps that read the current name
2. [ ] Ticket - file one ticket listing them and change nothing now [recommended]
3. [ ] Ignore - leave them as they are

### 1 of 1. One public response field in src/api/profile.ts uses the wrong name

### What was found
At `src/api/profile.ts:18`, the response uses `displayName` instead of `display_name`. No other card shares this file.

### Why it matters
The API naming rule in `AGENTS.md` requires public JSON response fields to use lowercase words separated by underscores. Existing clients consume `displayName`, so renaming it would change the public contract.

### What happens if you accept
Fix is unavailable because the proposed rename changes a public contract. Choosing Ticket would request one ticket describing the mismatch and leave the code unchanged; filing still requires separate exact-text approval.

Pick one:
1. [ ] Fix - unavailable: renaming the field changes the public contract used by existing clients
2. [ ] Ticket [recommended] - file one ticket listing the mismatch and change nothing now
3. [ ] Ignore - leave it as it is
